newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures higher, PV up on outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures higher, PV up on outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were higher Monday with Palo Verde (PV) contracts seeing the biggest gains amid regional power plant outages and some cooler weather, trade sources said.
"We had a move toward the upside. There are some outages and scheduled maintenance going on," said one trader.
Most of the activity was in March and second quarter PV contracts, he noted.
The March PV and Calfiornia Oregon border (COB) contracts will expire on Tuesday.
But traders expect the recent market strength to be short-lived, with the fundamentals still pretty bearish.
"The weather is not extremely bullish, there is a significant amount of water and plenty of natural gas," explained another trader.
He expected futures to resume a range-bound trading pattern.
Unless the eastern U.S. sees a significant cold spell, which would attract hub natgas, stored volumes are likely to be sold off, prompting lower prices, the trader said.

But support for power was seen from planned outages on Saturday of the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant and a 750 MW coal-fired unit at the Navajo power plant, both in Arizona, tightened regional supplies.
Meanwhile, a restart schedule for the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California remains uncertain after the discovery of a tube leak last week.
March California Oregon Border (COB) was settled up 27 cents at $10.57 per megawatt hour, while April COB settled unchanged at $9.95 per MWh.
March Palo Verde (PV) settled up 61 cents at $14.20, while April ended up 15 cents at $13.00 per MWh.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be three to six degrees Fahrenheit above normal through much of the week, although they were called to moderate to one to three degrees above normal by the end of the week. Little or no precipitation was expected through the week.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be four to eight degrees below normal through Tuesday and then moderate to near normal in the middle of the week. Above normal precipitation was expected.
